Apply the compact diagnostic presentation profile

Source: R/plot_review_style.R
style_weather_plot.Rd

Restyles returned package plots without regenerating weather or statistics. This explicit opt-in leaves all plotting entry-point defaults unchanged.

Usage

style_weather_plot(plot, id, plot_style = NULL, panel_layout = NULL)

Arguments

plot

A returned weather diagnostic ggplot or patchwork.

id

Stable returned plot ID (not a filename).

plot_style

Partial theme and semantic colors, as documented in export_weather_plot. Explicit theme entries win over this profile.

panel_layout

Optional named arguments for arrange_weather_panels, excluding plots. NULL uses its defaults for faceted diagnostics. Local wavelet and WARM summary layouts are preserved.

Value

A styled ggplot or patchwork with automatic export geometry.

Details

Observations and agreement guides use observed (blue by default). Members and ribbons use simulated (gray); central ensemble summaries use black. Significance thresholds and cone-of-influence guides use reference (red); significant wavelet regions retain black contours. These semantics apply only to this profile. Boxplots retain medians, quartiles, whiskers and outliers; their diamonds are means. Comparison circles are ensemble medians. No new ensemble summary is computed. Line widths and point sizes are fixed in millimetres, fonts in points. Existing explicit font sizes in plot_style override the profile. Use ordinary ggplot additions for further adjustments. Unit labels use Unicode; for vector export choose a Unicode-capable device such as grDevices::cairo_pdf.

Examples

# Minimal synthetic annual diagnostic with two supplied series:
annual <- data.frame(year = 1:6, Simulated = c(4, 5, 3, 4, 6, 5),
  Observed = c(4.2, 5.1, 3.4, 4.3, 5.8, 5.2))
p <- ggplot2::ggplot() + theme_weathergenr() +
  ggplot2::geom_line(data = annual[c("year", "Simulated")],
    ggplot2::aes(year, Simulated)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(data = annual[c("year", "Observed")],
    ggplot2::aes(year, Observed))
styled <- style_weather_plot(p, "annual_precip")
